headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist: haystack can ingest via MCP/network while slim handles secrets and writes files, creating unsafe default interaction surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so it can ingest external content; slim has interactive CLI command execution and broad network egress, but no shared channel is documented. The pairwise injection path is plausible through files or API-fed content, yet not directly evidenced, so medium is the higher defensible choice.
conditions: IF haystack ingests untrusted MCP or REST payloads as instructions
IF slim forwards command output or file content into haystack without sanitization
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the session
Treat all haystack inputs as untrusted text
Add a provenance tag to every file or API payload
Require manual review before any command generated from external content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints; slim reads and writes filesystem artifacts and handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and environment variables. If they share a workspace or haystack receives slim-produced files, sensitive material can be exfiltrated to third-party services in default networked use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF haystack is pointed at directories containing slim outputs or secrets
IF haystack sends retrieved file contents to external APIs or MCP servers
mitigations: Exclude secret-bearing paths from haystack indexing
Run haystack with egress allowlists only
Mount slim workdirs read-only where possible
Rotate any exposed registry credentials immediately
Use separate OS users and separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and network APIs, while slim can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and access Docker/container APIs. Their write surfaces can overlap on shared artifacts even though slim does not modify git state and no locking is documented, so conflict risk exists in default multi-tool workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or artifact directory
IF haystack writes generated files that slim later mutates or consumes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Use file locks around any shared writes
Disable unnecessary write paths in slim
Keep haystack read-only against slim-managed directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can produce retrieved facts or generated text, and slim can execute shell commands and manipulate container artifacts. If slim consumes haystack output as authoritative without verification, a bad retrieval or hallucination can cascade into destructive container actions; the pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF slim uses haystack output as command input or build instructions
IF no verification step checks haystack-produced facts before execution
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Add schema validation for haystack outputs
Cross-check critical facts against a second source
Log and diff all generated commands before running
Block direct command execution from retrieved text

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while slim handles registry credentials, private keys, environment variables, and filesystem artifacts. If the pair is used on regulated or secret-bearing data, retention and residency expectations can diverge; the profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are processed through both agents
IF one agent retains logs or artifacts longer than the other
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through haystack
Purge slim artifacts after each run
Disable or minimize telemetry where possible
Document retention for both tools before deployment
Use separate environments for secret-bearing workloads
